NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 12 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 29 · 9 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 26, 9:33 PM ET

Joe Burrow is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 12 DraftKings main slate at 23.3 DraftKings points for $7,700, against New Orleans. Trevor Lawrence (21.7, $6,700) and C.J. Stroud (20.5, $6,500) are next.

Jayden Daniels returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.38 projected points per $1,000 at $6,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 26, 9:33 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 12

Joe Burrow, CIN vs NO ($7,700)

Joe Burrow carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 23.3 DraftKings points at $7,700, the highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.5 points clear of Trevor Lawrence. The salary works out to 3.02 projected points per $1,000, 7th of 11 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Burrow averaged 23.3 points with a simulated floor of 9.3 and a ceiling of 43.3, and he holds 14% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cincinnati is a 10-point favorite at home against New Orleans, with an implied team total of 29.75 in a game totaled at 49.5.

Trevor Lawrence, JAX vs TEN ($6,700)

Trevor Lawrence projects 2nd at the position with 21.7 DraftKings points at $6,700, 2nd on the main slate overall. The model includes 3.5 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.24 projected points per $1,000, 3rd of 11 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Lawrence averaged 21.8 points with a simulated floor of 8.6 and a ceiling of 39.7, and he holds 23% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Jacksonville is a 14.5-point favorite at home against Tennessee, with an implied team total of 32 in a game totaled at 49.5.

Value: Anthony Richardson Sr., IND vs NYG ($4,800)

Anthony Richardson Sr. projects for 16.1 DraftKings points at $4,800, which works out to 3.36 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 11 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 6.3 rushing attempts. Across 50,000 simulations Richardson averaged 16.1 points with a simulated floor of 5.9 and a ceiling of 29.7, and he holds 3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Indianapolis is a 6-point underdog at home against the Giants, with an implied team total of 17.75 in a game totaled at 41.5.
